decision_table.name: Calculate_Net_Receipts
decision_table.description: Calculate net receipts from gross receipts minus returns and allowances. Form 1120 line 1c = 1a - 1b

rule.policy: Net receipts = Gross receipts - Returns and allowances. Reference: Form 1120 Instructions, Line 1c
No gross receipts = zero net receipts.

decision_table.name: Calculate_Gross_Profit
decision_table.description: Calculate gross profit from net receipts minus cost of goods sold. Form 1120 line 3 = 1c - 2

rule.policy: Gross profit = Net receipts - Cost of goods sold. Reference: Form 1120 Instructions, Line 3 Reference: Schedule A - Cost of Goods Sold
No receipts: gross profit = negative COGS (loss from inventory).

decision_table.name: Calculate_Total_Income
decision_table.description: Calculate total income (sum of all income sources). Form 1120 line 11

actions.action:
revenue.total_income = revenue.gross_profit + revenue.dividends_received + revenue.interest_income + revenue.gross_rents + revenue.gross_royalties + revenue.capital_gain_net_income + revenue.net_gain_loss_4797 + revenue.other_income;
// Copy to result entity for tax calculation result.total_income = revenue.total_income;

rule.policy: Total income = Gross profit (line 3) + Dividends (line 4) + Interest (line 5) + Rents (line 6) + Royalties (line 7) + Capital gain (line 8) + Net gain/loss Form 4797 (line 9) + Other income (line 10). Reference: Form 1120 Instructions, Line 11

decision_table.name: Calculate_Compensation_Deduction
decision_table.description: Calculate deduction for officer compensation. Form 1120 line 12

actions.action: // Officer compensation is fully deductible (subject to reasonableness test) // Reasonableness test is typically applied during audit, not in calculation

rule.policy: Compensation paid to officers is deductible under IRC Section 162(a)(1). Must be reasonable in amount and for services actually performed. Reference: Form 1120 Instructions, Line 12 Reference: IRC Section 162(a)(1) Reference: Reg. Section 1.162-7 (Compensation for personal services)
No officer compensation to deduct.

decision_table.name: Calculate_Interest_Deduction
decision_table.description: Calculate interest expense deduction with IRC 163(j) limitation. Form 1120 line 18

condition.name: exceeds_30pct_ati
condition.comment: Interest expense exceeds 30% of adjusted taxable income

actions.action: // Interest expense is fully deductible (under 163(j) limit)

rule.policy: Business interest expense is fully deductible when it does not exceed business interest income plus 30% of adjusted taxable income. Reference: Form 1120 Instructions, Line 18 Reference: IRC Section 163(j)

Business interest expense limited to 30% of adjusted taxable income per IRC 163(j). Excess interest carried forward indefinitely. Reference: Form 1120 Instructions, Line 18 Reference: IRC Section 163(j) Reference: Form 8990 - Limitation on Business Interest Expense
No interest expense to deduct.

decision_table.name: Calculate_Charitable_Contributions
decision_table.description: Calculate charitable contributions deduction with 10% limitation. Form 1120 line 19

rule.policy: Charitable contributions are fully deductible when they do not exceed 10% of taxable income (computed without the charitable deduction). Reference: Form 1120 Instructions, Line 19 Reference: IRC Section 170(b)(2)
Charitable contributions limited to 10% of taxable income per IRC 170(b)(2). Excess contributions carried forward 5 years. Reference: Form 1120 Instructions, Line 19 Reference: IRC Section 170(b)(2)
No charitable contributions to deduct.

decision_table.name: Calculate_Total_Deductions
decision_table.description: Calculate total deductions (sum of all deduction line items). Form 1120 line 27

actions.action: result.total_deductions = result.compensation + result.salaries_and_wages + result.repairs_and_maintenance + result.bad_debts + result.rents + result.taxes_and_licenses + result.interest_expense + result.charitable_contributions + result.depreciation + result.depletion + result.advertising + result.pension_profit_sharing + result.employee_benefit_programs + result.other_deductions;

rule.policy: Total deductions = Sum of lines 12-26 (all deduction categories). Reference: Form 1120 Instructions, Line 27

decision_table.name: Calculate_Taxable_Income
decision_table.description: Calculate taxable income (total income minus total deductions). Form 1120 line 28 = 11 - 27

rule.policy: Taxable income = Total income - Total deductions. Reference: Form 1120 Instructions, Line 28

Deductions exceed income: taxable income is zero. Net operating loss (NOL) may be available for carryforward/carryback. Reference: Form 1120 Instructions, Line 28 Reference: IRC Section 172 (NOL deduction)

decision_table.name: Apply_Corporate_Tax_Rate
decision_table.description: Calculate federal corporate income tax at 21% flat rate. Form 1120 line 31 = line 28 × 21%

rule.policy: Federal corporate income tax = Taxable income × 21% (flat rate). Rate established by Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) of 2017, effective 2018+. No progressive brackets. No Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT repealed for corporations). Reference: Form 1120 Instructions, Schedule J Line 2 Reference: IRC Section 11(b) - Tax imposed on corporations
No taxable income = no tax liability.

decision_table.name: Calculate_Refund_Or_Owed
decision_table.description: Calculate final refund or amount owed. Payments + Credits - Tax

rule.policy: If (Payments + Credits) > Tax: Refund If (Payments + Credits) < Tax: Amount owed Reference: Form 1120 Instructions, Lines 32-35 Line 32: Total payments and refundable credits Line 33: Estimated tax penalty (not implemented Phase 1) Line 34: Amount owed = Tax - Payments (if positive) Line 35: Overpayment = Payments - Tax (if positive)

decision_table.name: Calculate_RD_Credit
decision_table.description: Calculate research and development tax credit. Form 6765 - Credit for Increasing Research Activities

rule.policy:
Research & Development credit = 20% of qualified research expenses (QREs) exceeding base amount.
QREs include: - Wages for qualified research activities - Supplies used in research - Contract research expenses (65% of amount paid)
Base amount calculation requires 4-year average of prior QREs.
Reference: Form 6765 - Credit for Increasing Research Activities Reference: IRC Section 41 - Credit for increasing research activities Reference: Publication 561 - Determining Value of Donated Property
No qualified research expenses = no R&D credit.

decision_table.name: Calculate_General_Business_Credit
decision_table.description: Calculate general business credit (aggregate of all credits). Form 3800 - General Business Credit

condition.name: has_any_credits
condition.comment: Has at least one business credit

rule.policy:
General business credit = Sum of all component credits - Research & development credit (Form 6765) - Work opportunity tax credit (Form 5884) - Energy credits (not implemented) - Low-income housing credit (not implemented) - Other credits (not implemented)
Credit is limited to net income tax minus greater of: (1) Tentative minimum tax, or (2) 25% of net regular tax liability above $25,000
Unused credits carry back 1 year, forward 20 years.
Reference: Form 3800 Instructions Reference: IRC Section 38 - General business credit
No business credits available.

decision_table.name: Determine_Asset_Class
decision_table.description: Determine MACRS asset class and recovery period for depreciable property. Publication 946 - How to Depreciate Property

rule.policy:
MACRS asset classification determines recovery period and depreciation method.
Property Classes (Publication 946 Table B-1): - 3-year: Tractor units, racehorses 2+ years, breeding hogs - 5-year: Automobiles, computers, office equipment, breeding/dairy cattle - 7-year: Office furniture, fixtures, most machinery and equipment - 10-year: Vessels, barges, tugs, single-purpose agricultural structures - 15-year: Land improvements, gas stations, depreciable improvements - 20-year: Farm buildings, municipal sewers - 27.5-year: Residential rental property - 39-year: Nonresidential real property (commercial buildings)
Depreciation methods: - 200% declining balance (200DB) for 3, 5, 7, 10-year property - 150% declining balance (150DB) for 15, 20-year property - Straight-line (SL) for 27.5, 39-year property
Reference: Publication 946 - How to Depreciate Property Reference: IRC Section 168 - MACRS
If asset class not specified, default to 7-year property (most common).

decision_table.name: Calculate_Section_179
decision_table.description: Calculate Section 179 expense deduction for qualifying property. Form 4562 Part I - Election To Expense Certain Property

rule.policy:
Section 179 expense deduction allows immediate expensing of qualifying property.
2025 Limits: - Maximum deduction: $1,220,000 - Phaseout threshold: $3,050,000 (total property placed in service) - Phaseout: Dollar-for-dollar reduction above threshold
Qualifying property: - Tangible personal property (machinery, equipment, furniture, computers) - Off-the-shelf software - Qualified improvement property (QIP) - Must be used > 50% for business
Nonqualifying property: - Buildings and structural components - Land and land improvements - Property used outside the U.S. - Property used for lodging - Listed property used 50% or less for business
Limitation: Cannot exceed taxable income from business.
Reference: Form 4562 Instructions, Part I Reference: IRC Section 179 - Election to expense certain depreciable business assets Reference: Publication 946 Chapter 2
Property does not qualify for Section 179 deduction.
Section 179 annual limit exceeded. No additional deduction available.

decision_table.name: Calculate_Bonus_Depreciation
decision_table.description: Calculate bonus depreciation for qualifying property. Form 4562 Part II - Special Depreciation Allowance

condition.name: has_bonus_rate
condition.comment: Bonus depreciation rate is greater than zero

rule.policy:
Bonus depreciation allows additional first-year depreciation for qualifying property.
Phaseout schedule (TCJA): - 2022: 100% - 2023: 80% - 2024: 60% - 2025: 40% - 2026: 20% - 2027: 0% (expires)
Qualifying property: - New or used property (expanded by TCJA) - Original use begins with taxpayer OR acquired used property - MACRS property with recovery period of 20 years or less - Computer software - Qualified improvement property (QIP) - Placed in service during tax year
Nonqualifying property: - Property required to use Alternative Depreciation System (ADS) - Listed property used 50% or less for business - Property used for lodging
Election to opt out: Taxpayer can elect out of bonus depreciation.
Reference: Form 4562 Instructions, Part II Reference: IRC Section 168(k) - Special allowance for certain property Reference: Publication 946 Chapter 3
Property does not qualify for bonus depreciation.
Bonus depreciation rate is 0% for 2025 (phased out).

decision_table.name: Calculate_MACRS_Depreciation
decision_table.description: Calculate MACRS depreciation for property. Form 4562 Part III - MACRS Depreciation

condition.name: has_remaining_basis
condition.comment: Has remaining basis after Section 179 and bonus

rule.policy:
MACRS (Modified Accelerated Cost Recovery System) depreciation using IRS tables.
Depreciation methods by property class: - 3, 5, 7, 10-year: 200% declining balance (200DB) - 15, 20-year: 150% declining balance (150DB) - 27.5, 39-year: Straight-line (SL)
Conventions: - Half-year: Property placed in service mid-year (most property) - Mid-quarter: If > 40% of property placed in service in Q4 - Mid-month: Residential/nonresidential real property
First-year rates (half-year convention): - 3-year: 33.33% - 5-year: 20.00% - 7-year: 14.29% - 10-year: 10.00% - 15-year: 5.00% - 20-year: 3.75%
Full MACRS tables in Publication 946 Appendix A.
Reference: Form 4562 Instructions, Part III Reference: IRC Section 168 - MACRS Reference: Publication 946 Appendix A (MACRS Percentage Tables)
No remaining basis to depreciate (fully expensed via Section 179/bonus).

decision_table.name: Aggregate_Depreciation
decision_table.description: Aggregate all depreciation deductions for Form 1120. Form 4562 - Depreciation and Amortization

rule.policy:
Total depreciation deduction (Form 1120 line 20) equals: - Section 179 expense deduction (Form 4562 Part I) - Bonus depreciation (Form 4562 Part II) - MACRS depreciation (Form 4562 Part III) - Amortization (not implemented)
Reference: Form 4562 Line 22 Reference: Form 1120 Line 20

decision_table.name: Compute_Corporate_Tax_Return
decision_table.description: Main orchestration table for corporate tax calculation. Calls all income, deduction, and tax calculation tables in sequence.

rule.policy:
Corporate tax calculation flow (Phase 2 - with depreciation and credits):
1. Calculate income (Form 1120 lines 1-11) 2. Calculate depreciation (Form 4562): a. Section 179 expense deduction b. Bonus depreciation (phased out in 2025) c. MACRS depreciation 3. Calculate deductions (Form 1120 lines 12-27) 4. Calculate taxable income (Form 1120 line 28) 5. Apply 21% tax rate (Schedule J) 6. Calculate credits (Form 3800): a. R&D credit (Form 6765) b. General business credit 7. Determine refund or amount owed
Reference: Form 1120 - U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return Reference: Form 4562 - Depreciation and Amortization Reference: Form 3800 - General Business Credit Reference: Form 6765 - Research & Development Credit
